{"basis":"measured","fact_type":"finding","name":"MEASURED 2026-10-01: rmcp 3.5.0 (2026-09-28) moves ProtocolVersion::LATEST from 2025-11-25 to 2026-07-28 and adds LATEST_WITH_INITIALIZE; reflow2 (on 3.4.0) uses LATEST as its advertised version and as its initialize fallback, and its pin test will fail on the bump by design","source":"github.com/modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk releases rmcp-v3.4.1 and rmcp-v3.5.0, PR #1105; reflow2 origin/main 64b145a; ~/.cargo registry rmcp-3.4.0 src/model.rs:175","statement":"Raised by Anthony ("rmcp-v3.5.0 is out"). reflow2's Cargo.lock holds rmcp 3.4.0.

WHAT MOVED UPSTREAM:
- rmcp 3.4.1 (2026-09-23): the transport falls back after JSON discover rejections (#1288). That bears on fact:through-the-shared-proxy-a-2026-07-28-server-discover-is-answered-as-an-unreachable-server-2026-09-26.
- rmcp 3.5.0 (2026-09-28), Added: #1105 moves `ProtocolVersion::LATEST` to `V_2026_07_28` and adds `LATEST_WITH_INITIALIZE`. In 3.4.0 it is `V_2025_11_25` (model.rs:175).
- rmcp 3.5.0, Fixed:
  - float fields decoded through serde_json::Number (#1300);
  - duplicate sep-2243 headers rejected (#1274);
  - explicit default ports matched in the Origin allowlist (#1270);
  - an empty cacheScope tolerated instead of the whole result being silently dropped (#1281);
  - an explicit null structuredContent preserved in CallToolResult (#1295).

WHERE reflow2 USES LATEST:
- `ReflowService::describe_protocol_version()` returns it, and get_info advertises it (service.rs:6870, :7472).
- handshake.rs passes it as the server FALLBACK to `negotiate`, the copy of rmcp's pub(crate) rule (handshake.rs:150-194). A client asking for a version reflow2 supports is echoed. Any other request gets LATEST.

WHAT THE BUMP DOES, AND THE TEST THAT CATCHES IT:
- tests/tools.rs:935 `the_advertised_protocol_version_is_the_sdks_latest_and_is_pinned` asserts LATEST == V_2025_11_25, so the bump fails it ON PURPOSE ("decide deliberately whether reflow2 should follow it").
- Following it changes the advertised version to 2026-07-28, which matches what this requirement already claims.
- It ALSO moves the initialize fallback to a revision that is not initialize-based. That is what rmcp's new LATEST_WITH_INITIALIZE is for, so the fallback probably wants LATEST_WITH_INITIALIZE, not LATEST. Unverified until the upgrade is built and its tests run.

THE STANCE THIS REQUIREMENT TAKES: "A NEW REVISION is adopted deliberately … never inherited silently by a dependency bump". This is the case it describes, and the pin test is doing its job. Not done yet: the upgrade itself, as its own PR after v0.77.0.","subject_id":"req:reflow2-conforms-to-the-mcp-specification-revision-it-serves","valid_from":"2026-10-01"}
